Context/Background:
Intraductal papillary neoplasms (IPNs),  including intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs), intraductal oncocytic papillary neoplasms (IOPNs), and intraductal tubulopapillary neoplasms (ITPNs), are clinically detectable macroscopic non-invasive cyst-forming lesions, some of which progress to invasive pancreatic cancer. Proteins and glycoproteins have proven to be useful clinical biomarkers for classifying cyst-forming neoplasms in the pancreas.Here, we used proteomics and glycoproteomics to characterize a series of histologically and genetically well-characterized surgically resected IPNs, including IPMNs and IOPNs.

Our analysis included 69 IPNs (64 IPMNs and 5 IOPNs), 76 macro-dissected grossly normal duct tissues (NDs, with 32 of the 76 NDs coming from the same resection specimens as the IPNs), and 32 cyst fluid samples (22 from matched IPMN patients, 3 matched IOPN patients, 2 from unrelated IPMN patients, and 5 other cysts).
Prompt: Compare the differential genes on global proteome level and glycoproteome level for IPMN vs ND.  Provide a pathway level summary of biological functions of upregulated or downregulated glycopeptides whose global protein expression remained unchanged.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
The study compares global proteome and glycoproteome profiles in surgically resected IPMNs versus matched normal duct (ND) tissues. At the global proteome level (Table S2A; 9,417 proteins), significant up-regulation was dominated by immunoglobulin variable chains (e.g., IGLV3-10, IGKV1-27) and metabolic enzymes (e.g., SLC22A23), whereas many glycoproteins showed post-translational changes without concordant protein abundance shifts. At the glycoproteome level (Table S3I; 85 glycopeptides), 85 sites on 40 proteins were significantly altered (all Up.Sig in IPMN vs ND), including ANO9, ADAM10, ENTPD5, and a subset whose total protein levels were unchanged.

Keywords  
“Glycosylation,” “DDAH1,” “Cholesterol biosynthesis,” “Vesicle trafficking,” “Tetraspanin”

Candidate Genes  
DDAH1, ERLIN2, CPD, TSPAN13

Pathway Enrichments  
Because all glycopeptide changes were Up-regulated, ORA yields only “UP” enrichment. No KEGG_2016 pathways passed threshold; GO_Biological_Process_2023 and Reactome_Pathways_2024 had multiple enriched themes.

GO_Biological_Process_2023 (UP):  
| Theme                                           | Direction | Leading Genes |
|-------------------------------------------------|-----------|---------------|
| Regulation Of Cellular Response To Hypoxia      | UP        | DDAH1         |
| Citrulline Metabolic Process                    | UP        | DDAH1         |
| Arginine Catabolic Process                      | UP        | DDAH1         |
| SREBP Signaling Pathway                         | UP        | ERLIN2        |
| Regulation Of Sterol Biosynthetic Process       | UP        | ERLIN2        |

Reactome_Pathways_2024 (UP):  
| Theme                                                    | Direction | Leading Genes |
|----------------------------------------------------------|-----------|---------------|
| eNOS Activation                                          | UP        | DDAH1         |
| Metabolism of Nitric Oxide NOS3 Activation and Regulation| UP        | DDAH1         |
| FGFR1 Mutant Receptor Activation                         | UP        | ERLIN2        |
| Signaling by FGFR1 in Disease                            | UP        | ERLIN2        |
| RND1 GTPase Cycle                                        | UP        | CPD           |

Analysis  
Among glycoproteins with unchanged total abundance, DDAH1 glycosylation mapped to arginine/NO metabolism and hypoxia response, indicating altered vascular signaling. ERLIN2 glycosylation enriched sterol/cholesterol biosynthesis (SREBP pathway), suggesting membrane-lipid remodeling in IPMN. CPD glycosylation linked to Golgi-associated vesicle trafficking and Rho GTPase cycles, pointing to secretion pathway modulation. TSPAN13 showed significant glycosite changes but did not drive any enriched pathway, highlighting a potentially novel role in cell-surface organization distinct from bulk expression.

Targeted Subset (Arginine-related ORA terms)  
| Term                          | Genes  | Adjusted P-value |
|-------------------------------|--------|------------------|
| Arginine Catabolic Process    | DDAH1  | 0.00799          |
| Arginine Metabolic Process    | DDAH1  | 0.00799          |

Key Genes/Proteins (Leading-edge)  
Up:  
| Gene     | Direction  | Role/Function                                  | Pathway(s)                                                 |
|----------|------------|------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| DDAH1    | Glyco-Up   | Dimethylarginine dimethylaminohydrolase        | Arginine Catabolism; eNOS Activation; Hypoxia Response     |
| ERLIN2   | Glyco-Up   | ER lipid-raft protein regulating SREBP/sterol   | SREBP Signaling; Cholesterol Biosynthesis                  |
| CPD      | Glyco-Up   | Carboxypeptidase in Golgi                      | RND GTPase Cycle; Golgi-Associated Vesicle Biogenesis      |
| TSPAN13  | Glyco-Up   | Tetraspanin family cell-surface protein        | Not observed in enriched pathways                          |

Down: none observed

Comparisons & Confidence  
Global proteome changes were dominated by immune variable chains; glycoproteome changes reveal post-translational modulation in metabolic and trafficking pathways (high confidence). TSPAN13 glycosylation is a single-modality finding (lower confidence) needing further validation.

Implications  
Enhanced glycosylation of DDAH1 and ERLIN2 may reprogram NO signaling and cholesterol homeostasis, respectively, promoting cyst growth or microenvironment remodeling in IPMN. CPD glycosylation changes implicate altered secretion/processing of bioactive peptides.

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate glycosylation-driven activity changes by site-specific mutagenesis of DDAH1 and ERLIN2.  
2. Measure NO levels and sterol content in IPMN versus ND tissues to link glycosylation to function.  
3. Investigate CPD’s role in vesicular trafficking of growth factors in IPMN models.  
4. Explore TSPAN13 glycosylation impact on cell adhesion and signaling in cyst-forming lesions.

Explicit Checks  
– Cell-cycle themes: not observed at glyco-only level (none enriched).  
– Hypoxia/stress response: present (GO:1900037).  
– Metabolism: arginine and sterol processes enriched.  

References  
None (no PMIDs were retrieved via literature-mining tools).
